title.narrative: Improving Family Health through access to safe water and sanitation

description.narrative: ACLO Chuquisaca is a Jesuit NGO focusing on community development in peri-urban areas in the city of Sucre. An estimated 70% of Sucre’s population are migrants from the poorest rural areas of the departments of Chuquisaca and Potosi. These migrants have settled in popular urban neighbourhoods of Sucre and lack basic services such as water, electricity, and proper drainage. Many of these neighbourhoods are not recognised by the municipal government and so the people living there are excluded from decision-making spaces and the development of municipal public policy which has a direct affect on their lives This WASH project forms part of the Water and Gender Match Fund programme. The project aims to help the communities to set up drinking water, sanitation systems and eco-latrines, improve their knowledge and practice of safe water consumption and hygiene and lobby for support from municipal governments in replicating the activities more widely. There will be a particular emphasis on working with women to empower them to play a key role in changing practice in the family and community domains to increase convenient availability of drinkable water and improve hygiene and sanitation
